ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Hippocrates Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing care with a comprehensive geriatric assessment, after his annual wellness screening elsewhere noted slower walking and a near-fall: gait speed, Timed Up and Go, chair stands, balance, grip strength, MoCA, GDS-15, hearing, vision, nutrition and continence; frailty; a deprescribing review; bone health; what matters most to him; and a geriatric medicine consultation. Concerns: He wants to keep walking into town to teach, and to manage his stairs at home; Knee pain on stairs and on the hill, and a near-fall on his stairs that frightened him; He wants no medicine he does not need. [S]

tr.td: Establishing care with a comprehensive geriatric assessment, after his annual wellness screening elsewhere noted slower walking and a near-fall: gait speed, Timed Up and Go, chair stands, balance, grip strength, MoCA, GDS-15, hearing, vision, nutrition and continence; frailty; a deprescribing review; bone health; what matters most to him; and a geriatric medicine consultation
Two-week review, seen the same day by geriatric medicine: the cause of the slower gait, knee osteoarthritis, the deprescribing plan, a strength and balance program, falls prevention and bone health
Eight-week review: knee pain and function, the strength and balance program, sleep without diphenhydramine, the DXA result and pneumococcal vaccine
Four-month review: knee function, repeat gait, balance and strength measures, vitamin D, falls and the home program
Seven-month review: knee function, mobility, falls, medicines, vaccines and what matters most to him
Same-day sick visit for a common cold

Comprehensive geriatric assessment at intake: gait speed, Timed Up and Go, 30-second chair stand, four-stage balance test, grip strength, orthostatic blood pressure, MoCA, GDS-15, hearing (whisper test), vision, nutrition (MNA-SF), continence, the Clinical Frailty Scale and the FRAIL scale; what matters most to him (4Ms)
Geriatric medicine consultation for slower gait and a near-fall in a man of 89: the cause, frailty, the deprescribing plan, falls prevention, bone health and a plan built on what matters most to him

Deprescribing (Beers 2023): stop over-the-counter naproxen (chronic NSAID use at 89) and diphenhydramine (strongly anticholinergic); acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day as needed; sleep routine without a sleep aid; check every over-the-counter purchase with the clinic or pharmacist
Bone health: 25-hydroxyvitamin D at intake and after repletion; vitamin D3 1,000 units daily; calcium from food (about 1,200 mg a day); DXA of the spine and hips with FRAX

Knee osteoarthritis: diagnosis on clinical criteria without X-ray; exercise as the core treatment; diclofenac 1% gel to the knees; acetaminophen as needed; KOOS JR and a pain score at each visit; weight kept steady

Falls prevention (STEADI and the World Falls Guidelines): twelve weeks of physical therapy with a progressive strength and balance program based on Otago, then tai chi twice a week; a home safety check with a second stair rail and night lights; well-fitting shoes; gait, balance and strength measures repeated after the program

Low bone mass below treatment thresholds (FRAX hip 2.6 percent, major 11 percent): no osteoporosis medicine now; vitamin D, dietary calcium, exercise and falls prevention; repeat DXA and FRAX in two years, or sooner after any fracture
Find out why he walks more slowly and nearly fell
Knee osteoarthritis with reduced quadriceps strength and balance, and diphenhydramine at night; no neurologic, thyroid, B12 or blood pressure cause
Walk into town and back for his teaching without stopping to rest, and climb his stairs safely
Gait speed 0.78 to 0.96 m/s; Timed Up and Go 13.8 to 10.9 seconds; walks to town without stopping; no falls
No medicine he does not need, and none on the Beers list
Naproxen and diphenhydramine stopped; sleeping without a sleep aid; chose not to take a cold remedy with diphenhydramine
Knee pain 3 of 10 or less on stairs
5 to 2 of 10 on exercise, topical diclofenac and acetaminophen as needed; KOOS JR 62 to 74
Bones and falls: vitamin D above 30 ng/mL and no falls
Vitamin D 24 to 33 ng/mL; no falls in seven months
